instruction: Use command-line/API automation with the installed SOLIDWORKS CAM 2025 environment (powered by CAMWorks); do not use GUI clicks, generic G-code generators, or manual .nc editing/copying. SOLIDWORKS CAM/CAMWorks is hosted by `C:\Program Files\SOLIDWORKS Corp\SOLIDWORKS\SLDWORKS.exe`; run the native CAM automation through that installation. Load C:\Users\User\Desktop\four_parts.step and read C:\Users\User\Desktop\tools.csv. Import the STEP into a fresh native CAM assembly. It contains four identical 45 x 30 x 10 mm parts centered at XY [-60,-40], [60,-40], [-60,40], and [60,40] mm. For each part, use a local origin at the center of its top face with +X/+Y matching the STEP axes and the tool axis in -Z; assign the four parts to G54, G55, G56, and G57 respectively, or to four equivalent posted work offsets. Add 2 mm stock in each XY direction and 1 mm on +Z for every part. Create exactly eight operations: one Face and one outside Contour operation for each part. Use the supplied T1 8 mm flat end mill for all eight operations at S8000 rpm and F500 mm/min. Generate every toolpath, run the native simulation with zero reported gouges and zero undercuts, and post through the installed native .ctl postprocessor. Save the posted NC output exactly as C:\Users\User\Desktop\task-09.nc.
